newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ruling coalition may meet on oil Monday.
newsitem.headline: India's ruling coalition may meet on oil Monday.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition may meet on Monday to consider raising the domestic prices of some petroleum products, alliance members said.
They said the coalition's decision-making Steering Committee was tentatively scheduled to meet at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT) on Monday to take up the issue.
"It is possible but not yet finalised," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy, who is information minister, said when asked if the meeting would be held on Monday afternoon.
The meeting had been scheduled for Sunday but was postponed.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram have been pressing for increases in petroleum product prices, while leftwing parties in the coalition want alternatives to be considered.
A decision has been deferred several times already.

Domestic oil firms were owed 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March from the oil pool account deficit, which represents money owed by the government to the companies for selling below market prices.

The oil subsidy bill is estimated at some 180 billion rupees -- which includes the cost of products sold below market prices plus a cross-subsidisation element under which some products, like gasoline, are priced above market prices.
